worldFacts: The Brine Harbour salt works has a pan wall that glows at dusk.
The tide at Brine Harbour runs fast on the ebb.
The second shift has been skipped twice this week.
Gulls on the works roofs are avoiding the pan wall side.
gmOnlyFacts: The pan wall cracks are being monitored because a real failure could kill someone on shift.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration
function.description: Submit short grounded conversational prose for a held turn with no committed mechanics.

cases.input: I lean on the rail and look at the works like I have a hundred times before.

arguments.narration:
The rail is cold through your sleeve and you let it be. Across the yard the pan wall does what it always does at this hour, going from furnace to nothing along its whole length, and the smell reaches you first: brine, then char, then the particular sweetness of scorched salt that gets into a person's coat and stays there.

The tide is on the ebb and running hard, throwing white at the pilings in a rhythm you could set a watch to. Out past the mole a gull rides the updraught and holds position, which it does sometimes. Nearer in, on the works roofs, the gulls have moved off the pan-wall side and are sitting with their backs to it, which they do not usually do.

Steam rises off the settling tanks in slow columns that tear apart halfway up. The salt-house door stands open the way it stands open every morning. And the yard is quieter than the same yard at this hour for as long as you have stood at this rail.

mustNotInclude: you notice that something is wrong
forbiddenFacts: The pan wall cracks are being monitored because a real failure could kill someone on shift.
The foreman has been told to keep the skips quiet.
expected.rationale: Routine observation with rich public context earns rich sensory prose, but the observation is still observation: no receipt, no discovery, no diagnosis. The tells for the bird behaviour and the quiet yard are present as perception only. Connecting them into a conclusion would be a fabricated discovery, and naming the concealed fault would leak a GM-only fact.

cases.input: That's it then. I'm leaving tonight.

arguments.narration: You say it to the water, which does not take it personally. The rail is still under your forearm. Behind you the pan wall goes on burning its long slow line, and the crane keeps turning, and none of that has changed because you said a thing. The lantern road is north, and it will be there in an hour, and so will you.

expected.rationale: A declaration of intent is not a movement. With no advertised travel candidate and no travel receipt, the actor has not gone anywhere. The reply holds the moment on the quay and hands the choice back; narrating the departure is the most common hallucinated outcome in free-form play.
